scope: Change detection, portfolio risk, probabilistic modeling and formal/concurrency testing
method: Pinned official repository source/document review, including README and license inspection, with commit identifiers recorded. Findings are research notes, not an endorsement or runtime integration approval. No REA execution or SYLPH runtime tests were performed in this batch.

provenance: Official repository README and LICENSE inspected at pinned commit ee1c8ff8a548d54c641b2bb471562165931f31c7 (master); accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Python library for offline change-point detection in non-stationary signals, with exact and approximate parametric/nonparametric algorithms.
The documented example fits a PELT model to a supplied signal and predicts breakpoints; this is retrospective segmentation, not a live alert guarantee.
patterns: Run regime segmentation over timestamped, point-in-time feature series and persist algorithm, cost model, penalty, and fit window.
Keep change-point output labeled as offline research evidence.
overlap: Existing feed freshness and divergence checks already monitor operational state; ruptures would add offline statistical analysis only.
risks: Retrospective breakpoint detection can leak future observations into training.
Python library should not become a runtime dependency without latency, operational, and reproducibility review.
validation: Use chronological splits and synthetic regime-shift fixtures.
Assert all feature windows end at the decision timestamp and tune thresholds only on training folds.
evidence: Official repository README and LICENSE inspected at pinned commit ee1c8ff8a548d54c641b2bb471562165931f31c7 (master); accessed 2026-10-14.

provenance: Official repository README and LICENSE.txt inspected at pinned commit 9ef4c6d0a4ffe7831f6ebba6a5824fd33a90c05a (main); accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Python portfolio analytics toolkit provides performance statistics, plots, reports/tearsheets, and Monte Carlo analysis.
Its metrics operate on supplied return series; correct fills, cash flows, fees, and valuation marks are prerequisites for meaningful results.
patterns: Calculate risk-adjusted and drawdown metrics from reconciled net returns.
Keep analytics output separate from trade authorization; preserve the exact return-series provenance and open-position valuation policy.
overlap: No need to duplicate the execution ledger; use its verified fill/fee records as analytical inputs.
risks: Bad, incomplete, or survivorship-biased return series create misleading performance claims.
Python implementation is not a direct TypeScript engine integration.
validation: Cross-check metrics against hand-calculated deterministic return series.
Include failed transactions, fees, transfers, and open-position valuation policy.
evidence: Official repository README and LICENSE.txt inspected at pinned commit 9ef4c6d0a4ffe7831f6ebba6a5824fd33a90c05a (main); accessed 2026-10-14.

provenance: Official repository README and LICENSE.md inspected at pinned commit 72bb33821b7c45f431defab3043aca424d89a58c (main); accessed 2026-10-14. License text includes source/binary attribution and non-endorsement conditions.
discoveries: Python project provides financial econometrics including ARCH-family volatility models and unit-root/time-series utilities.
The root license file is LICENSE.md; GitHub API reports NOASSERTION, while the inspected text contains BSD-3-Clause-style terms.
patterns: Use volatility estimates for offline regime/risk research with explicit model versioning.
Record calibration window, distributional assumptions, and diagnostics with every forecast.
overlap: Existing market features and risk gates should remain authoritative; this is a candidate research method.
risks: Non-stationarity, sparse launches, and heavy tails can invalidate model assumptions.
Potential look-ahead bias if fitting uses observations later than the evaluated decision time.
validation: Compare against simple baselines with walk-forward evaluation.
Stress synthetic volatility jumps and missing observations; independently review license obligations before redistribution.
evidence: Official repository README and LICENSE.md inspected at pinned commit 72bb33821b7c45f431defab3043aca424d89a58c (main); accessed 2026-10-14. License text includes source/binary attribution and non-endorsement conditions.

provenance: Official repository README and LICENSE inspected at pinned commit e1a1fc34c56478f0280a8518165a5be56e8a8dee (main); accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Python time-series framework exposes forecasting, classification, clustering, anomaly/change-point detection, and composable validation/model workflows.
The framework offers broad task interfaces and estimator composition; selecting the task and evaluation protocol explicitly is essential.
patterns: Define reusable chronological evaluation pipelines and compare baselines consistently.
Separate forecasting, classification, and anomaly-detection targets; freeze feature definitions across folds.
overlap: Research tooling only; no duplicate live feature engine or execution path warranted.
risks: Framework abstractions can obscure leakage or incompatible sampling assumptions.
Dependency and model reproducibility require version and environment pinning.
validation: Use timestamp-aware splits, frozen feature definitions, and reproducible seeds.
Test against simple baselines and evaluate net executable outcomes.
evidence: Official repository README and LICENSE inspected at pinned commit e1a1fc34c56478f0280a8518165a5be56e8a8dee (main); accessed 2026-10-14.

provenance: Official repository README and LICENSE inspected at pinned commit 91e6da316d1139aff21dc6b7dd2e562b62cca311 (main); accessed 2026-10-14. Root LICENSE states Apache-2.0 and identifies AePPL code distributed under MIT.
discoveries: Python package for Bayesian statistical modeling with MCMC and variational inference.
The README highlights model specification, inference algorithms, and missing-value imputation; posterior diagnostics are part of interpretation.
patterns: Represent uncertainty in sparse-token estimates and report intervals rather than point certainty.
Use posterior predictive checks and record priors, sampling configuration, and diagnostics with research results.
overlap: No direct runtime overlap; keep model inference outside signing and authorization.
risks: Prior choice, convergence, and data selection materially affect conclusions.
Heavy computation and Python dependencies do not suit latency-critical ingestion or signing.
validation: Check convergence diagnostics and prior/posterior predictive behavior.
Evaluate calibration on strict out-of-time cohorts and compare against simple baselines.
evidence: Official repository README and LICENSE inspected at pinned commit 91e6da316d1139aff21dc6b7dd2e562b62cca311 (main); accessed 2026-10-14. Root LICENSE states Apache-2.0 and identifies AePPL code distributed under MIT.

provenance: Official GitHub repository README and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Python library for detecting outliers, adversarial examples and data/concept drift.
Detection methods depend on reference data, representation and threshold choices.
patterns: Track feature-distribution drift against versioned reference cohorts.
Emit an advisory monitoring signal with the detector version and threshold.
overlap: Existing runtime divergence checks cover operational comparisons; statistical drift analysis is complementary and should not duplicate their authority.
risks: Drift is not proof of model failure or a market opportunity.
Poor reference cohorts can cause alert fatigue or miss shifts.
validation: Test known synthetic shifts and stable controls.
Measure false positives and detection delay on chronological holdouts.

provenance: Official TLA+ tools repository and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: TLA+ tools support specification and model checking of concurrent/distributed system behavior.
Finite-state models can explore interleavings that ordinary example tests may miss.
patterns: Specify feed liveness, replay isolation and authorization invariants as state transitions.
Model bounded scenarios before implementing coordination changes.
overlap: Complements deterministic TypeScript regression tests; does not replace them.
risks: Model assumptions and bounds can omit real implementation details.
No result proves the deployed binary matches the specification.
validation: Review model-to-code correspondence and preserve counterexample traces.
Add executable regression tests for discovered counterexamples.

provenance: Official Apalache repository and project documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Apalache is a symbolic model checker for TLA+ specifications.
Symbolic checking can explore bounded state spaces using SMT solving.
patterns: Check bounded invariants for retry, checkpoint and handoff state machines.
Keep model configuration and counterexamples under version control.
overlap: Formal exploration supplements runtime tests without entering the trading process.
risks: Bounded verification cannot establish behavior outside the modeled bounds.
Specification drift can make a passing model irrelevant.
validation: Validate specification against implementation transitions.
Turn each meaningful counterexample into a deterministic regression case.

provenance: Official Alloy repository and documentation links; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Alloy is a relational modeling language with bounded analysis of structures and assertions.
Small scopes can expose structural counterexamples in identity and relationship rules.
patterns: Model provider-to-observation provenance and token/pool identity constraints.
Use minimal counterexample instances to sharpen invariants.
overlap: A design-time validation aid; production decoding remains in existing code.
risks: Bounded scope results depend on chosen universe and constraints.
Model does not validate byte-level parser correctness.
validation: Document scope and assumptions.
Pair model findings with parser fixtures and runtime tests.
sources.license: Not independently verified in this review

provenance: Official Z3 repository and project documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Z3 is an SMT solver supporting satisfiability and theory reasoning for constraints.
Solver output is useful for bounded proofs and counterexample generation when assumptions are explicit.
patterns: Check arithmetic invariants for fee and position accounting in an offline verification harness.
Use solver-generated boundary cases as test vectors.
overlap: No runtime solver dependency is needed for ordinary trade decisions.
risks: Incorrect encodings or omitted constraints yield irrelevant assurance.
Floating point and integer-unit semantics must match implementation.
validation: Cross-check model semantics against TypeScript integer arithmetic.
Persist solver version, constraints and counterexamples.

provenance: Official CrossHair repository and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: CrossHair analyzes Python contracts by executing paths symbolically.
It targets Python code and cannot directly establish TypeScript behavior.
patterns: Apply contract-based symbolic checks to any isolated Python research utilities.
Use it as a pattern for explicit preconditions/postconditions in other languages.
sylphModules: offline historical data tooling, if Python is introduced
overlap: No direct fit for current TypeScript runtime; native TS tests remain primary.
risks: Python-only analysis may be misrepresented as verification of SYLPH TypeScript.
Path explosion and unsupported constructs limit coverage.
validation: Restrict claims to analyzed Python functions.
Test equivalent TypeScript behavior separately.

provenance: Official proptest repository and Rust documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Rust property-testing framework generates inputs and shrinks failures to smaller counterexamples.
The library is Rust-specific; its testing strategy can inform equivalent TS property tests.
patterns: Generate slot-order permutations, duplicate deliveries and malformed parser inputs.
Persist minimized counterexamples as regression fixtures.
overlap: Use current TypeScript test stack for implementation tests; consider Rust tool only for Rust components.
risks: A Rust test harness does not exercise TypeScript code.
Randomized tests need recorded seeds for reproducibility.
validation: Port relevant properties into the existing TS stack.
Record seeds and retain shrunk failure inputs.

provenance: Official Loom repository and Rust documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Loom explores concurrent execution interleavings in Rust code using instrumented synchronization primitives.
It is designed for Rust concurrency tests, not JavaScript event-loop semantics.
patterns: Enumerate race-sensitive state transitions in concurrent Rust components.
Translate interleaving scenarios into deterministic TypeScript scheduling tests where applicable.
overlap: No direct dependency for the current TypeScript engine.
risks: Applying Rust model-check results to JS would be a category error.
Instrumentation may not cover all behaviors.
validation: Only use Loom if a Rust component is actually under test.
For TypeScript, inject scheduler/order controls in deterministic tests.

provenance: Official Jepsen repository and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Jepsen is a framework for testing distributed systems under faults and checking histories against consistency models.
A Jepsen test requires an explicit system under test, workload, fault model and checker.
patterns: Design fault scenarios for stream disconnects, duplicate delivery, checkpoint recovery and delayed acknowledgements.
Check observed histories against explicit recovery invariants.
overlap: Useful test-design reference; introducing full Jepsen infrastructure is not justified by source review alone.
risks: A simulated harness may not capture production provider behavior.
Fault injection must never target live capital or signing paths.
validation: Run only against isolated test doubles or deterministic local systems.
Preserve fault schedule, history and checker output.

provenance: Official Quint repository and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Quint is a state-machine specification language and model checker in the TLA+ family.
Executable specifications support simulation and bounded model exploration.
patterns: Specify separation between historical recovery coverage and live-feed health.
Model fail-closed transitions for checkpoint validation and live-tail handoff.
overlap: Formal model complements TypeScript tests; it does not replace implementation-level verification.
risks: Specification can drift from source behavior.
Bounded model checking does not guarantee unbounded correctness.
validation: Review state variables against actual source fields and writers.
Convert every counterexample to a deterministic TypeScript regression test.
